records.title: Artifact validity under varying agent configurations in LLM-assisted software development: A comparative analysis
records.rationale: Abstract is truncated but title and opening explicitly frame a comparative analysis of artifact validity across differing LLM agent configurations over the development lifecycle, which is exactly the single-agent versus multi-agent configuration question in RQ2. Journal venue (Information and Software Technology) indicates an empirical software engineering study.

records.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
records.rationale: Studies the principles that determine performance of LM-based agent systems as they scale, which bears directly on RQ2's conditions where adding agents helps or hurts, though the truncated text does not confirm a software engineering task setting. Preprints are eligible under the protocol.

records.title: AI BIM coordinator for non-expert interaction in building design using LLM-driven multi-agent systems
records.rationale: A named LLM-driven multi-agent architecture with specialist coordination roles, but the application domain is BIM/building design rather than a software engineering activity and the truncated text shows no single-agent versus multi-agent comparison. Useful only as cross-domain evidence on role specialization and coordination design.

records.title: LLM-assisted development of Rust for high-performance bioinformatics software: practices, workflows, and boundaries
records.rationale: Reports concrete agentic-coding failure modes from building a real Rust tool, naming layer misidentification, semantic drift during script migration, and goal substitution inside agentic loops, which map to RQ3 failure-mode categories. Also documents a tiered workflow (specification-driven design, test-driven development, multi-model parallel exploration) and compiler-based verification as mitigation.

records.title: The Jadescript Language for Event-Driven, Agent-Oriented Programming
records.rationale: Jadescript is a JADE-derived agent-oriented programming language for classical industrial multi-agent systems with no LLM component, matching the preregistered exclusion for non-LLM agents. Reliability framing is about language design, not LLM agent coordination.

records.title: Human-AI experience in integrated development environments: a systematic literature review
records.rationale: Systematic review of 90 studies on AI-assisted coding inside IDEs that quantifies verification overhead, over-reliance, and correctness/maintainability/security risks, supplying single-assistant baseline evidence for RQ1's verification and reliability strand. It is not multi-agent, so it informs the comparison rather than answering it.

records.title: A Multi-agent LLM System for Automated Requirements Analysis: A Study on User Story Generation and Prioritization
records.rationale: Investigates a role-based multi-agent LLM system for a requirements engineering activity (user story generation and prioritization), matching the SE activity plus named architecture inclusion rule. Role assignment across agents is the exact specialization mechanism under study in RQ2.

records.title: A Multi-Agent System for Complex Reasoning in Radiology Visual Question Answering
records.rationale: Evaluates a specialized LLM/MLLM multi-agent pipeline (context understanding, multimodal reasoning, answer validation) against strong single-model MLLM baselines on hard cases, qualifying under the any-domain single-versus-multi inclusion rule. The dedicated validation agent and hallucination framing are relevant to RQ3 verification mechanisms.

records.title: An LLM-Enhanced Multi-agent Architecture for Conversation-Based Assessment
records.rationale: Presents an LLM multi-agent architecture for conversation-based student assessment, an education task rather than a software engineering activity, and the truncated text reports no single-agent comparison. Retained only as background on dialog-driven multi-agent architectures.

records.title: No skin in the game: why agentic AI requires principal-agent governance
records.rationale: Argues that delegating tasks to LLM-based agents creates principal-agent asymmetries and proposes a dual-layer Agent/Governor architecture with a monitoring engine, structural constraints, and an accountability ledger. It is a governance position paper without software engineering evaluation, so it informs RQ1's accountability and observability discussion rather than the performance comparison.

records.title: A Large language model-based multi-agent manufacturing system for intelligent shopfloors
records.rationale: Truncated abstract describes an LLM-based multi-agent system responding to dynamic shopfloor disturbances, a manufacturing control domain with no software engineering task and no stated single-agent baseline. Relevant only as an example of LLM multi-agent orchestration under disturbance.

records.title: Power-Aware Orchestration for Geo-Distributed LLM Inference via Quantum Optimization
records.rationale: Concerns datacenter-level scheduling of LLM inference requests using a QAOA-based integer program; the 'orchestration' is request routing, not coordination among LLM agents, and no software engineering activity or agent configuration comparison is present.

records.title: Large language models in power systems toward cognitive intelligence: A literature review
records.rationale: Truncated text confirms a review of LLM applications to renewable-rich cyber-physical grid operations, which is neither a software engineering activity nor a single-agent versus multi-agent configuration comparison. Fails both inclusion clauses.

records.title: Large Language Model Agents
records.rationale: Textbook-style chapter covering theoretical and practical foundations of LLM agents and multi-agent systems, offering definitional framing but no empirical results, benchmark, or software engineering case. Useful only for terminology and taxonomy grounding.

records.title: Decentralized Marketplace for Large Language Model Merging, Buying Models, Selling Models, Fine-Tuning of Models
records.rationale: Describes a marketplace for parameter-fusion model merging and fine-tuning (SLERP, TIES, DARE, Task Arithmetic); the 'agents' are trading/model artifacts, not coordinating LLM agents performing software engineering tasks. No single-versus-multi agent comparison is reported.

records.title: Leveraging LLMs for the Quality Assurance of Software Requirements
records.rationale: Empirical RE 2024 study where a single LLM assesses requirements against ISO 29148 quality characteristics, explains its decisions, and proposes rewrites, validated with practising software engineers. Provides a single-agent quality-assurance baseline for the requirements-side comparison in RQ2.

records.title: Vibe Modeling: Challenges and Opportunities
records.rationale: The recovered text is a generic motivational opening about software complexity rather than a substantive abstract, so judgement rests on the title: a position piece on LLM-driven ('vibe') software modeling with challenges enumerated. Relevant as design-phase framing but contributes no empirical or comparative evidence.

records.title: ChatGPT for good? On opportunities and challenges of large language models for education
records.rationale: Education-focused opportunity/challenge commentary on LLMs with no software engineering activity and no agent configuration comparison; the truncated text confirms a general AI-in-education framing. Fails both inclusion clauses.

records.title: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
records.rationale: The recovered text is NOT an abstract; it is the ISSTA 2024 front-matter welcome message with dates, location, and co-location details. The record is a whole-proceedings container rather than a primary study, so it is excluded.

records.title: A design science research approach to Large Language Model-Based Agents for Requirements Specification (LLMBA4RS) in low-code applications
records.rationale: Presents a named LLM agent method (LLMBA4RS) built on RAG and the CrewAI multi-agent framework for generating and refining user stories, demonstrated and evaluated by practitioners across three low-code applications. Combines a software engineering activity, a named multi-agent architecture, and practitioner evaluation.

records.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Smart Educational Services: A Comprehensive Review
records.rationale: A review of LLMs for personalized and interactive educational services; no software engineering activity is addressed and the proposed conceptual framework is pedagogical rather than an agent-coordination architecture. Fails both inclusion clauses.

records.title: Automation of systematic literature reviews: A systematic literature review
records.rationale: Published in 2021, which violates the preregistered pre-2022 cutoff, and its automation techniques predate LLM-based agents. Any methodological value for review conduct does not satisfy the inclusion criteria.

records.title: Multi-Agent Programming

records.title: Empirical Research in Software Engineering — A Literature Survey
records.rationale: A 2018 mapping study of empirical methods in software engineering, which fails the pre-2022 cutoff and involves no LLM agents. It is methodological background on experiment/case-study/survey practice only.

records.title: The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
records.rationale: The recovered text is NOT an abstract; it is a 2017 Springer book marketing description of GDPR compliance guidance. Pre-2022, no LLM agents, and no software engineering agent comparison.

records.title: Software Agent Systems
records.rationale: The recovered text is NOT a real abstract but a truncated promotional blurb praising agents as a fascinating topic. The 2015 chapter predates the cutoff and covers classical software agent systems rather than LLM-based agents.

records.title: Autonomous agents modelling other agents: A comprehensive survey and open problems
records.rationale: A 2018 AIJ survey of classical agent-modelling techniques (game-theoretic and learning-based), which fails the pre-2022 cutoff and the non-LLM agent exclusion. Its open problems concern opponent modelling, not LLM agent coordination.

records.title: Differential Privacy
records.rationale: Dwork's 2006 privacy foundations paper on statistical database disclosure limitation; pre-2022 and entirely unrelated to LLM agents or software engineering agent configurations. Likely pulled in by a citation-snowballing edge.

records.title: An Introduction to Agile Methods
records.rationale: A 2004 Advances in Computers chapter introducing agile development practices, far predating the 2022 cutoff and containing no LLM or agent-architecture content. The recovered text is a truncated editorial-style blurb rather than a structured abstract.
